# The integral lattice generated by simple affine gradients

This internal support unit defines `simpleDerivativeLattice Ψ C`, the
integer span in the real dual translation space of the gradients of the
simple affine roots of `C`. The predicate `HasIntegralSimpleDerivativeSpan Ψ C`
means that every root of the full derivative system belongs to that lattice.
Multipliable derivative roots are included.

The implemented proof first proves that each simple affine reflection
preserves the lattice. On a simple generator the difference from its
pullback is an integer multiple of the reflecting simple gradient, by
the affine root system's integral coroot-pairing axiom. Integer span
induction extends this to the lattice. A root stabilizer applied to the
set of affine functionals with gradient in the lattice then extends
preservation to the subgroup generated by the chamber wall reflections.
Involutivity gives preservation in both directions for each generator.

The existing indivisible-root conjugacy proof constructs its conjugating
map in precisely this subgroup, although the earlier public conclusion
records only root preservation. The strengthened
`exists_simple_eq_comp_or_neg_mem_wallClosure` retains that membership:
use the imported gallery conjugacy of a coroot reflection to a chamber
wall reflection, then identify its pulled-back indivisible root with a
simple root up to sign. The positive multiple is one by the imported
indivisible-root proportionality theorem.

Consequently each indivisible affine gradient belongs to the simple
derivative lattice: its conjugate is a simple gradient up to sign, and
pullback by the inverse conjugating map preserves the lattice. Under
the explicit `HasIndivisibleDerivativeLifts Ψ` premise this applies to
every full derivative root and proves
`hasIntegralSimpleDerivativeSpan_of_indivisible_lifts`.

All assertions retain the rank-zero-compatible affine root system
hypothesis and the prescribed regular chamber. The translation space
and its affine torsor have independent universe parameters. The proof
uses no irreducibility, transitivity, reducedness, actual group,
valuation or characteristic hypothesis.

This is derived infrastructure, justified by the imported integral
pairing axiom and gallery/orbit theorems, rather than a transcription
from literature. It does not prove the actual-group indivisible-lift
premise, identify a finite root base after deleting a node, compare an
absolute Cartan matrix, or prove the anisotropic affine-diagram target.
